rules.expected: Use the original complete G1 dication identity and the supplied mapped neutral CB7/CB8 host graphs. Form 1:1 CB7:G1 and 1:2 CB8:G1 complexes. Generate independent host–guest placements; the added bound source coordinates are withheld. Counterions are excluded consistently. Use one aqueous continuum convention. Label each guest atom G_A/id or G_B/id and host H/id. The required states are vertical optical/electronic prerequisites. Their comparison alone does not predict emission wavelength or fluorescence efficiency without excited-state relaxation and kinetics. Compare transition energies/oscillator strengths and matched guest transition densities at identical guest coordinates for full-host, deleted-host and deleted-partner controls. Bright/dark splitting is E(bright)-E(dark) with both state identities recorded; host deletion measures combined host response, not purely electrostatics. Reject wrong host ring size/guest charge, source bound coordinates used as discovered minima, comparisons with relaxed versus frozen geometries silently mixed, or calling total host response exclusively electrostatic. Static transition properties do not prove fluorescence quantum yield.
